stem: At this rate, how many hours will the drone take to photograph the entire wetland?
stimulus: On a survey map, 1 centimeter represents 0.5 kilometer. A wetland shown on the map has an area of 12 square centimeters. A drone photographs the wetland at a constant rate of 2,500 square meters per minute. (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
explanation: Area scales by the square of the linear scale factor. Each square centimeter on the map represents $(0.5\text{ km})^2 = 0.25\text{ km}^2$, so the wetland's real area is $12 \times 0.25 = 3\text{ km}^2$. Changing square kilometers to square meters also uses a squared factor: $3 \times (1{,}000)^2 = 3{,}000{,}000\text{ m}^2$. The drone takes $\frac{3{,}000{,}000\text{ m}^2}{2{,}500\text{ m}^2/\text{min}} = 1{,}200$ minutes, and $\frac{1{,}200}{60} = 20$ hours.

A.why: You squared the map scale correctly, but then converted $3\text{ km}^2$ to square meters by multiplying by $1{,}000$ instead of $1{,}000^2$. That gives $3{,}000\text{ m}^2$, which takes 1.2 minutes, or 0.02 hours. Kilometers to meters is a linear factor too, so for area it has to be squared.

C.why: You applied the map scale once ($12 \times 0.5 = 6$) instead of squaring it. That doubles the real area to $6\text{ km}^2$ and gives 40 hours. For area, each square centimeter stands for $0.5^2 = 0.25\text{ km}^2$.

D.why: 1,200 is the time in minutes. The question asks for hours, so you still need to divide by 60.

stem: What is the greatest number of pipes in this rank that can sound at the same time?
stimulus: A pipe organ's blower supplies air at a rate of 25 cubic feet per minute, but 10% of that air is lost through leaks before it reaches the pipes. While it sounds, each pipe in one rank of the organ uses 9 cubic inches of air per second. (1 foot = 12 inches)
explanation: Volume scales by the cube of the linear factor, so $1\text{ ft}^3 = 12^3 = 1{,}728\text{ in}^3$. Convert only the 'per minute' part of the rate to seconds: $\frac{25 \times 1{,}728\text{ in}^3}{60\text{ s}} = 720\text{ in}^3/\text{s}$. After the 10% leak, $0.9 \times 720 = 648\text{ in}^3/\text{s}$ reaches the pipes. Since $\frac{648}{9} = 72$, at most 72 pipes can sound at once.

A.why: You converted cubic feet to cubic inches with $12^2 = 144$ instead of $12^3 = 1{,}728$. That gives $\frac{25 \times 144}{60} \times 0.9 = 54\text{ in}^3/\text{s}$, and $\frac{54}{9} = 6$. Volume needs the linear factor cubed.

C.why: You converted the units correctly to $720\text{ in}^3/\text{s}$ but left out the 10% leak. Only 90% of that air, $648\text{ in}^3/\text{s}$, reaches the pipes.

D.why: You converted the volume correctly but never changed 'per minute' to 'per second'. This compares a per-minute supply with a per-second demand. Write the units next to each number and the seconds won't cancel, which shows you need to divide by 60.

stem: Which of the following is closest to the total mass, in kilograms, of ink the printmaker uses for the run?
stimulus: A printmaker inks a rectangular plate that measures 20 inches by 34 inches. A 1-inch border along every edge of the plate is left uninked, and ink is applied to the rest of the plate at a rate of 1.5 grams per square foot for each impression. The printmaker pulls 200 impressions. (1 foot = 12 inches, 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
explanation: The border comes off both ends of each side, so the inked area is $(20-2)$ by $(34-2)$, or $18 \times 32 = 576$ square inches. A square foot is $12^2 = 144$ square inches, so the inked area is $576 \div 144 = 4$ square feet. Each impression uses $4 \times 1.5 = 6$ grams, so 200 impressions use $1{,}200$ grams, which is $1.20$ kilograms.

B.why: You used the whole $20 \times 34 = 680$ square-inch plate and forgot that the border is never inked. That gives $680 \div 144 \times 1.5 \times 200 \approx 1{,}417$ grams.

C.why: You divided 576 square inches by 12 instead of by $12^2 = 144$, so you got 48 square feet instead of 4. When you convert an area, you have to square the linear factor.

D.why: You treated 576 square inches as 576 square feet and never converted, because the rate is given per square foot. That gives $576 \times 1.5 \times 200 = 172{,}800$ grams.

stem: What is the minimum number of sensors the network must have to meet the requirement?
stimulus: A seismology team is placing sensors across a rectangular region that measures 25 miles by 40 miles. Regional guidelines require at least 1 sensor for every 32 square kilometers of the region. (1 mile = 1.6 kilometers)
explanation: Convert each side before you multiply. $25$ miles is $40$ km and $40$ miles is $64$ km, so the area is $40 \times 64 = 2{,}560$ square kilometers. You get the same result by multiplying $1{,}000$ square miles by $1.6^2 = 2.56$. Then $2{,}560 \div 32 = 80$ sensors.

A.why: You divided 1,000 square miles by 1.6 instead of multiplying, which turns the conversion around. That gives 625, and $625 \div 32 \approx 19.5$, so you rounded up to 20.

B.why: You divided 1,000 square miles by 32 as though the guideline were per square mile. That gives about 31.3, which rounds up to 32.

C.why: You multiplied 1,000 square miles by 1.6 only once. An area needs the factor squared, $1.6^2 = 2.56$, so you got 1,600 square kilometers instead of 2,560.

stem: How many additional residents would the district need to reach the target density?
stimulus: A city plan sets a target density of 6,000 residents per square kilometer for a rectangular district that measures 2.5 miles by 1.6 miles. The district currently has 30,000 residents. (1 mile = 1.6 kilometers)
explanation: The district is 4 square miles. Each square mile is $1.6^2 = 2.56$ square kilometers, so the district is $4 \times 2.56 = 10.24$ square kilometers. At the target density, that is $10.24 \times 6{,}000 = 61{,}440$ residents. The district already has 30,000, so it needs $61{,}440 - 30{,}000 = 31{,}440$ more.

A.why: You converted 4 square miles with the linear factor once and got 6.4 square kilometers. The target would then be 38,400, and subtracting 30,000 gives 8,400. You need to multiply by $1.6^2$, not 1.6.

B.why: This is the target density rewritten per square mile, $6{,}000 \times 2.56$. It is a rate, not a number of additional residents.

D.why: This is the total population the district needs at the target. You didn't subtract the 30,000 residents who already live there.

stem: At this rate, how many grams of sweat does the athlete lose per hour?
stimulus: In a heat-chamber trial, a sports scientist measures an athlete's sweat rate as 0.5 milligram per square centimeter of skin per minute. The athlete's body surface area is 1.8 square meters. (1 meter = 100 centimeters, 1 gram = 1,000 milligrams)
explanation: One square meter is $100^2 = 10{,}000$ square centimeters, so 1.8 square meters is $18{,}000$ square centimeters. Each minute, the athlete loses $0.5 \times 18{,}000 = 9{,}000$ milligrams, which is 9 grams. Over 60 minutes, that is $9 \times 60 = 540$ grams.

A.why: You turned 1.8 square meters into 180 square centimeters by using the linear factor of 100 once. The area factor is $100^2 = 10{,}000$.

B.why: Nine grams is the loss per minute. The question asks for the loss per hour, so you still need to multiply by 60.

D.why: You divided milligrams by 100 instead of 1,000 when converting to grams, so your answer is ten times too large.

stem: Based on these measurements, which of the following is closest to the total number of T cells in the patient's blood?
stimulus: A patient's blood contains 2,000 lymphocytes per cubic millimeter, and 60% of these lymphocytes are T cells. The patient's total blood volume is 5,000 cubic centimeters. (1 centimeter = 10 millimeters)
explanation: There are $0.6 \times 2{,}000 = 1{,}200$ T cells per cubic millimeter. One cubic centimeter is $10^3 = 1{,}000$ cubic millimeters, so that is $1.2 \times 10^6$ T cells per cubic centimeter. Multiply by 5,000 cubic centimeters: $1.2 \times 10^6 \times 5 \times 10^3 = 6 \times 10^9$.

A.why: You multiplied by the linear factor 10 only once. A volume conversion needs the factor cubed, $10^3$.

B.why: You squared the linear factor and got 100 cubic millimeters per cubic centimeter. Squaring is right for area, but volume needs the factor cubed, which gives 1,000.

D.why: You converted the volume correctly but counted every lymphocyte. Only 60% of them are T cells.

stem: How many minutes does the transfer of the full reel take?
stimulus: A music archive holds a reel of 1,800 feet of magnetic tape. The concert on it was recorded at a tape speed of 15 inches per second. To capture faint detail, an archivist digitizes the whole reel at half the recording speed. (1 foot = 12 inches)
explanation: Convert only the length and leave the 'per second' alone. 1,800 feet is $1{,}800 \times 12 = 21{,}600$ inches. Half of 15 inches per second is 7.5 inches per second, so the transfer takes $21{,}600 \div 7.5 = 2{,}880$ seconds. Dividing by 60 gives 48 minutes.

A.why: You divided 1,800 feet by 7.5 inches per second without converting feet to inches first. That gives 240 seconds, or 4 minutes.

B.why: You did the conversion correctly but used the recording speed of 15 inches per second. The transfer runs at half that speed, so it takes twice as long.

D.why: This is the transfer time in seconds. The question asks for minutes, so you still need to divide by 60.

stem: What is the minimum number of whole cubic yards of concrete the contractor must order?
stimulus: A contractor is pouring a rectangular concrete slab that is 36 feet long, 27 feet wide, and 6 inches thick. To allow for spillage, the order must be at least 5% more than the slab's volume. Concrete is sold only in whole cubic yards. (1 yard = 3 feet, 1 foot = 12 inches)
explanation: Six inches is 0.5 foot, so the slab's volume is $36 \times 27 \times 0.5 = 486$ cubic feet. One cubic yard is $3^3 = 27$ cubic feet, so the slab is $486 \div 27 = 18$ cubic yards. Adding 5% gives $18 \times 1.05 = 18.9$ cubic yards. Because concrete comes in whole cubic yards, the contractor must order 19.

A.why: Eighteen cubic yards is exactly the slab's volume. It doesn't include the 5% allowance, so it falls short of the 18.9 cubic yards required.

C.why: You divided by $3^2 = 9$ instead of $3^3 = 27$, which treats a volume like an area. That gives 54, and adding 5% gives 56.7, which you rounded up to 57.

D.why: You divided 486 cubic feet by the linear factor 3 only once. That gives 162, and adding 5% gives 170.1, which you rounded up to 171.

stem: Based on the survey, what is the estimated number of adult terns nesting on the island?
stimulus: An ornithologist surveys a colony of terns on a rectangular island that measures 0.3 kilometer by 0.12 kilometer. Only 40% of the island's area is suitable for nesting, and the suitable area holds an average of 0.6 nest per square meter. Each nest is tended by 2 adult terns. (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
explanation: The island is $300$ meters by $120$ meters, which is $36{,}000$ square meters. The suitable area is $0.4 \times 36{,}000 = 14{,}400$ square meters, which holds $0.6 \times 14{,}400 = 8{,}640$ nests. With 2 adults per nest, that is $17{,}280$ adult terns.

A.why: You changed 0.036 square kilometer to 36 square meters by multiplying by 1,000 once. An area needs $1{,}000^2 = 1{,}000{,}000$.

B.why: This is the number of nests. The question asks for adult terns, and each nest has 2 of them.

D.why: You used the whole island's area. Only 40% of it is suitable for nesting.
